scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Bugg developed in Sweden in the mid-1940s, influenced by Lindy Hop, swing, and rock 'n' roll.
Nils-Håkan Carlzon is credited as a pioneer who refined the style at the Nerikes Dance Institute.
Competitive Bugg began in the mid-1970s, initially as a single 'freestyle' class, before evolving into the current social and competitive formats.
on_screen: Map: Sweden · Europe
Image 1 with attribution

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Bugg is both a social dance and a competitive sport.
It is highly popular in Swedish dance clubs and at events featuring 'dansbands.' It serves as a primary social outlet for many in the Swedish dance community.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage — MISSING (use images)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Bugg is an improvised partner dance in 4/4 time.
The leader guides the follower counter-clockwise around the room.
The leader uses a 1-2-3-4 step pattern, while the follower steps on every beat.
Watch for Kick Ball Change, Ronde Ball Change.
on_screen: Hero video full screen, 30–45 s (gJCkfkExuQ8)
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Counter-clockwise movement around the room.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Bugg is danced to popular music from the swing family, including pop music from the 1960s to the present.
The tempo typically ranges from 120 to 180 beats per minute (30–45 bars per minute).
The pulse is 4/4 at about 150 beats a minute.
Upbeat pop music in 4/4 time suitable for swing-style movement.

scenes.title: Try one step
narration: Before we go, one step. Leader: Step left on beat 1 or 3, step right on beat 2 or 4.
Follower: Step on every beat, left foot on 2 and 4, right foot on 1 and 3.
Count it: 1-2-3-4 then 5-6-7-8 (eight counts, two bars).
Chapter 1 takes it slowly from here.
